name: FIToFIPaymentStatusReport
label: FI to FI Payment Status Report
summary: Tells the previous agent what happened to a payment it sent — accepted, rejected, pending, or settled. The feedback channel of the interbank flow.
whenUsed: Sent in response to a pacs.008, pacs.009 or pacs.003, either because the scheme mandates confirmation (instant-payment schemes require one within seconds) or because something went wrong. Also the message behind SWIFT gpi tracking updates. Can report on a whole group, on a payment-information block, or on individual transactions — and a single report can mix outcomes, which is what PART at group level means.
gotchas: The status codes separate 'accepted' from 'settled' and it is easy to conflate them. ACSP means in flight. ACSC means the debtor's side settled. ACCC means the creditor was credited. Releasing goods on ACSP is a real financial exposure.

A rejection without a usable reason code is the most common quality complaint about this message. ISO makes StsRsnInf optional; schemes make it mandatory for RJCT, and NARR with free text should be a last resort.
Original Group Information refers to the message you are reporting on, not to this one. OrgnlMsgId must echo the GrpHdr.MsgId of the inbound pacs.008 exactly or the sender cannot match the response.

fields.name: Message Identification
fields.note: This status report's own id — not the id of the payment being reported on.

fields.name: Instructing Agent
fields.note: The agent sending the status — usually the one that received the original payment.

fields.name: Original Group Information And Status
fields.note: Identifies the message being reported on, and optionally gives a single verdict for the whole thing.

fields.name: Original Message Identification
fields.note: Must exactly echo the GrpHdr.MsgId of the original. This is the matching key.

fields.name: Original Message Name Identification
fields.note: Which message type is being reported on, e.g. pacs.008.001.08. Needed because the same id space is shared across message types.

fields.name: Group Status
fields.note: Verdict for the entire original message. PART means mixed outcomes — you must then read the per-transaction statuses.

fields.name: Additional Information
fields.note: Free text, 105 characters per occurrence. Mandatory in practice when the reason code is NARR.

fields.name: Transaction Information And Status
fields.note: One block per payment being reported on.

fields.name: Status Identification
fields.note: Reference for this status record itself, so a later enquiry can cite it.

fields.name: Original Group Information
fields.note: Per-transaction restatement of which original message this came from — needed when one report covers several originals.

fields.name: Original End To End Identification
fields.note: The debtor's reference. What the originating customer will recognise.

fields.name: Original UETR
fields.note: The single most reliable matching key, because it is the one reference guaranteed not to change along the chain. Mandatory under CBPR+.

fields.name: Status Reason Information
fields.note: Why. Repeating, because several things can be wrong at once.

fields.name: Originator
fields.note: Which agent in the chain raised this reason — essential when a rejection is relayed back through intermediaries.

fields.name: Charges Information
fields.note: Charges applied in the course of processing the original payment.

fields.name: Acceptance Date Time
fields.note: When the payment was accepted. For instant schemes this is the timestamp the customer sees as the payment time.

fields.name: Effective Interbank Settlement Date
fields.note: When settlement actually happened, if it differed from what was requested.

fields.name: Original Transaction Reference
fields.note: A copy of the original payment's key details — amount, parties, agents. Lets the receiver verify it is matching the right payment without looking up its own records, which is invaluable when the references do not line up.
